purpose.title: Save a city: source interpretation
purpose.text: A request to save one supported city. It carries a city selector, not a complete Place; the HTTP save result is separate from later message delivery.

identity.title: Save a city: source interpretation
identity.text: This request has no durable request ID in the captured shape. cityId selects Place.id. A new outbox event gets a separate Guid; a 200 response is not an acknowledgement of Kafka publication or forecast readiness.

meaning.title: Save a city: source interpretation
meaning.text: The selected city key sent by the browser. This request carries only cityId; Places derives the Place name and coordinates from its supported-city lookup. It is not an event ID, and it is not a client-supplied Place object.

mapping.title: Save a city: source interpretation
mapping.text: The declared POST /places JSON body requires cityId, one of oslo, helsinki or lisbon, and disallows extra properties. This is the receiving contract, not proof that Dashboard validates the request.

representations.label: Places SavePlace DTO
representations.requiredness: Read when the captured Save handler runs
representations.nullability: Framework binding/rejection paths are not established here

mapping.title: Save a city: source interpretation
mapping.text: The declared JSON cityId corresponds to SavePlace.CityId; Save reads request.CityId and passes it to City(). Framework request binding is not an observed runtime result.

representations.label: Supported-city selector → Place.id
representations.typeLabel: string selector for the returned Place
representations.requiredness: A matching supported city is needed for the Save branch
representations.nullability: An unsupported key returns null from the lookup

mapping.title: Save a city: source interpretation
mapping.text: CityId selects a literal Place from City(). Place.id is the supported city key, while name, latitude and longitude come from the lookup constants. No request name or coordinate is forwarded into those values.

usage.condition: A captured city button is clicked
usage.coveredScope: Captured Save a city source ranges only; no publisher or forecast consumer expansion
usage.unresolved: Browser execution and HTTP delivery are unverified.

claim.title: Save a city: source interpretation
claim.text: The city buttons carry oslo, helsinki or lisbon in data-city. Their click handler sends JSON {cityId: button.dataset.city} to POST /api/places; it sends no name or coordinates. The browser later checks response.ok, not the returned Place fields.

usage.condition: Dashboard savePlace runs; the URL is selected by PLACES_URL or its fallback
usage.coveredScope: Captured Save a city source ranges only; no publisher or forecast consumer expansion
usage.unresolved: Actual deployment routing, request binding, receiver completion and timeout outcome are unverified. Whole-object forwarding does not prove validation.

claim.title: Save a city: source interpretation
claim.text: Dashboard serializes request.body as a whole and sends POST to ${placesUrl}/places. PLACES_URL overrides the base; its source fallback and selected Compose value are http://places:8080, giving POST http://places:8080/places. The handler has no named cityId validation. Fetch, response JSON or the 10-second timeout can reach 503 PLACES_UNAVAILABLE; that does not prove rollback or a safe retry.

usage.condition: The captured Save handler has been invoked with its bound DTO
usage.coveredScope: Captured Save a city source ranges only; no publisher or forecast consumer expansion
usage.unresolved: Framework model-binding failures and runtime dispatch are outside the shown body; this is source interpretation.

claim.title: Save a city: source interpretation
claim.text: If the Places Save handler runs, it passes request.CityId to City(). Only oslo, helsinki and lisbon map to a Place; a null lookup result returns 400 UNSUPPORTED_CITY without calling Save. The returned name and coordinates are lookup-derived, not request fields.

claim.title: Save a city: source interpretation
claim.text: Place.Id is explicitly bound to places.id in INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id. Only a newly inserted row calls InsertRequest, which serializes the complete Place into request_outbox.payload.place and inserts it in the same transaction. An existing city leaves both the stored Place and outbox unchanged; the transaction still commits. SQL, serialization or commit failure prevents normal completion of this shown Save path.

claim.title: Save a city: source interpretation
claim.text: After awaited Save returns normally, Places returns Ok(city), including this Place.Id value. Dashboard forwards the upstream status and parsed JSON without a response.ok check. The city-button handler checks HTTP success but does not read the returned Place fields; it displays "City saved; forecast pending" and then makes a separate weather read. Both a newly saved city and an existing city can return 200; this is not forecast or message-delivery completion. The separately bound declared HTTP 200 schema requires JSON.id; this is distinct from the event-envelope contract and does not prove runtime conformance.
